title: Comparative in Silico Investigation of Grapevine (Vitis vinifera) Leaf and Exocarp Phytochemicals in Kawasaki Disease Through Integrated Network, Molecular Modeling and Evidence-Weighted Target Ranking Framework Analyses
content: Kawasaki disease (KD) is an acute systemic vasculitis and the leading cause of acquired heart dis-ease in children, highlighting the need for alternative therapeutic strategies, particularly for pa-tients resistant to intravenous immunoglobulin therapy. This study comparatively investigated the therapeutic potential of Vitis vinifera leaf and fruit exocarp phytochemicals against KD using an integrated in silico framework consisting of network pharmacology, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and an evidence-weighted target ranking model. After ADME screening, three leaf-derived and seven exocarp-derived bioactive compounds were retained for analysis. Network pharmacology identified 127 overlapping KD-associated targets for the leaves and 109 for the fruit exocarp, with both datasets demonstrating significant protein–protein interaction en-richment. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics analyses revealed stable interactions of quercetin with AKT1 and myricetin with MMP9, supporting their potential therapeutic relevance. Multi-objective target prioritization further identified biologically relevant and druggable candi-date targets. Overall, the findings suggest that V. vinifera contains promising multi-target phyto-chemicals capable of modulating key inflammatory pathways involved in Kawasaki disease and provide a computational foundation for future experimental validation and therapeutic develop-ment.
